Other common functions: count, in_array (pass true for strict), array_key_exists, isset, array_keys/array_values, array_merge, array_slice, usort, ksort, implode/explode, json_encode/json_decode.

OOP: Classes, Interfaces, Traits, Abstract, Static

  • Classes have visibility (public/protected/private), typed properties, constructors (__construct) and magic methods (__toString, __get, __call…). A class can extend only one parent.
  • Interfaces declare method contracts and constants. A class can implement many interfaces.
  • Abstract classes can mix implemented methods with abstract ones and cannot be instantiated.
  • Traits let you reuse code horizontally. The trait's methods are copied into the class (use LoggerTrait;), and conflicts are resolved with insteadof/as. Java has nothing exactly like this; default methods in interfaces are the closest.
  • Static members belong to the class: self:: refers to the defining class and static:: uses late static binding (the called class). parent:: calls the parent's method.
  • final blocks extension or overriding. #[\Override] (8.3) asserts that a method really overrides a parent method.
interface Billable { public function total(): float; }

trait Timestamps {
    public ?\DateTimeImmutable $createdAt = null;
    public function touch(): void { $this->createdAt = new \DateTimeImmutable(); }
}

abstract class Document {
    abstract public function render(): string;
    public static function create(): static { return new static(); }
}

final class Invoice extends Document implements Billable {
    use Timestamps;
    public function render(): string { return 'Invoice'; }
    public function total(): float { return 100.0; }
}

Namespaces, Composer & PSR-4

Namespaces (namespace App\Billing;) prevent name clashes, and use imports a class. Composer is the dependency manager, playing the role Maven/Gradle plays in Java. composer.json lists your dependencies, composer.lock pins exact versions (commit it), and vendor/autoload.php is the generated autoloader.

PSR-4 maps a namespace prefix to a directory. With the config below, App\Billing\Invoice loads from src/Billing/Invoice.php, so you never write require for each class.

{
  "require": { "php": ">=8.2", "twig/twig": "^3.0" },
  "autoload": { "psr-4": { "App\\": "src/" } }
}

// public/index.php
<?php
require __DIR__ . '/../vendor/autoload.php';
use App\Billing\Invoice;
$inv = new Invoice();

Useful commands: composer install (install from the lock file, used in CI), composer update (resolve newer versions), composer dump-autoload -o (optimized classmap for production). Other PSRs worth knowing: PSR-1/PSR-12 (coding style), PSR-3 (logger), PSR-7/PSR-15 (HTTP messages and middleware), PSR-11 (container).

PHP 8.x Features

  • 8.0: named arguments, match expression (strict comparison, returns a value, no fall-through, throws UnhandledMatchError), nullsafe ?->, constructor property promotion, union types, attributes #[Route('/x')], throw as an expression, str_contains/str_starts_with, and the JIT.
  • 8.1: enums (pure and backed, with from()/tryFrom()/cases()), readonly properties, first-class callable syntax strlen(...), never, intersection types, fibers, new in initializers.
  • 8.2: readonly classes, DNF types, true/false/null as standalone types, dynamic properties deprecated.
  • 8.3: typed class constants, #[\Override], json_validate(), deep cloning of readonly properties.
  • 8.4: property hooks (get/set logic declared on the property), asymmetric visibility (public private(set)), new Foo()->bar() without extra parentheses, array_find/array_any/array_all, and the #[\Deprecated] attribute.
// PHP 8.4 property hooks + asymmetric visibility
final class Person
{
    public private(set) string $id;           // readable everywhere, writable only inside

    public string $email {
        set(string $value) {
            $this->email = strtolower(trim($value));
        }
    }

    public string $display {
        get => "{$this->id}: {$this->email}";  // virtual property
    }

    public function __construct(string $id, string $email)
    {
        $this->id = $id;
        $this->email = $email;                 // runs the set hook
    }
}

$len = strlen(...);                            // first-class callable (8.1)
echo $len('abc');                              // 3

Errors & Exceptions

PHP 7+ has a Throwable interface with two branches. Exception is for application errors (RuntimeException, InvalidArgumentException, PDOException, JsonException…). Error is for engine problems (TypeError, ValueError, DivisionByZeroError, ArgumentCountError). PHP has no checked exceptions.

Warnings and notices (for example an undefined array key) are not exceptions by default. Frameworks usually convert them with set_error_handler → ErrorException, and set_exception_handler acts as the global catch-all. In production, log errors (log_errors=On) and never show them (display_errors=Off), because stack traces can leak paths, SQL or PHI.

try {
    $data = json_decode($body, true, flags: JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);
    $repo->save($data);
} catch (JsonException | ValueError $e) {
    http_response_code(400);
} catch (PDOException $e) {
    $logger->error('DB failure', ['exception' => $e]);
    throw new RuntimeException('Could not save', previous: $e);
} finally {
    $lock->release();
}

PDO, Prepared Statements, Sessions & Security

PDO is the database abstraction layer that ships with PHP. Prepared statements send the SQL and the values separately, so user input is never parsed as SQL. This is the main defense against SQL injection. Table and column names cannot be bound as parameters, so check them against a whitelist.

$pdo = new PDO('mysql:host=db;dbname=emr;charset=utf8mb4', $user, $pass, [
    PDO::ATTR_ERRMODE            => PDO::ERRMODE_EXCEPTION,
    PDO::ATTR_DEFAULT_FETCH_MODE => PDO::FETCH_ASSOC,
    PDO::ATTR_EMULATE_PREPARES   => false,
]);

$stmt = $pdo->prepare('SELECT id, fname FROM patient_data WHERE lname = :lname');
$stmt->execute(['lname' => $_GET['lname'] ?? '']);
$rows = $stmt->fetchAll();

$pdo->beginTransaction();
try { /* several writes */ $pdo->commit(); }
catch (Throwable $e) { $pdo->rollBack(); throw $e; }
  • Sessions: session_start() sets a session-ID cookie, and the data lives on the server (files, Redis, DB) in $_SESSION. Call session_regenerate_id(true) after login to prevent session fixation.
  • Cookies: setcookie() with an options array. Set secure, httponly and samesite (Lax/Strict).
  • XSS: escape all output for its context, e.g. htmlspecialchars($s, ENT_QUOTES | ENT_SUBSTITUTE, 'UTF-8') for HTML. A Content-Security-Policy header adds defense in depth.
  • CSRF: generate a random token (bin2hex(random_bytes(32))), store it in the session, put it in every form and check it with hash_equals() on POST.
  • Passwords: password_hash($pw, PASSWORD_DEFAULT) (bcrypt, or Argon2id via PASSWORD_ARGON2ID) and password_verify(). Use password_needs_rehash() to upgrade old hashes. Never use md5 or sha1.

Twig Templating

Twig (from the Symfony project) compiles templates to PHP classes and caches them. It has three delimiters: {{ ... }} prints a value, {% ... %} runs a tag (if, for, block, extends, include, set, macro), and {# ... #} is a comment. Filters transform values with a pipe: {{ name|upper }}, |date('Y-m-d'), |default('-'), |length, |join(', '), |json_encode, |e('js').

Autoescape is on (HTML strategy) by default, so {{ comment }} is escaped automatically. |raw turns escaping off. Use it only for trusted, already-sanitized HTML. Inheritance: a child template {% extends %} a base layout and overrides named {% block %}s. {{ parent() }} keeps the parent block's content.

{# base.html.twig #}
<html><head><title>{% block title %}EMR{% endblock %}</title></head>
<body>{% block content %}{% endblock %}</body></html>

{# patients.html.twig #}
{% extends 'base.html.twig' %}
{% block title %}Patients - {{ parent() }}{% endblock %}
{% block content %}
  <ul>
  {% for p in patients %}
    <li>{{ p.name|title }} - {{ p.dob|date('d M Y') }}</li>
  {% else %}
    <li>No patients found</li>
  {% endfor %}
  </ul>
{% endblock %}

// PHP side
$twig = new \Twig\Environment(new \Twig\Loader\FilesystemLoader('templates'), [
    'cache' => '/tmp/twig', 'autoescape' => 'html',
]);
echo $twig->render('patients.html.twig', ['patients' => $rows]);

PHP vs Java

  • Runtime: PHP is interpreted per request (with OPcache and optional JIT) and keeps no state between requests. Java is compiled to bytecode and runs in a long-lived JVM with JIT and shared in-memory state.
  • Typing: PHP is dynamic with optional type declarations checked at runtime. Java is statically typed and checked at compile time. PHP has no generics in the language; PHPStan/Psalm add them through docblocks like @param list<Patient>.
  • Concurrency: PHP gets concurrency from many processes (FPM workers). Java uses threads, executors and virtual threads in one process.
  • Ecosystem: Composer/Packagist vs Maven/Gradle; Laravel/Symfony vs Spring; PHPUnit vs JUnit; Doctrine/Eloquent vs JPA/Hibernate; Twig/Blade vs Thymeleaf/JSP.
  • Similar OOP: classes, interfaces, abstract classes, exceptions, namespaces (≈ packages). PHP adds traits and magic methods. Java has checked exceptions, overloading and generics.

Closures, Arrow Functions and Generators

$rate = 0.18;
// closure: captures outer variables explicitly, by value
$withTax = function (float $p) use ($rate): float { return $p * (1 + $rate); };
// arrow fn (7.4+): captures outer scope automatically, by value, single expression
$withTax2 = fn(float $p): float => $p * (1 + $rate);
$counter = 0;
$inc = function () use (&$counter) { $counter++; };   // by reference

// generator: lazy sequence, constant memory
function readRows(string $file): Generator {
    $h = fopen($file, 'r');
    try {
        while (($row = fgetcsv($h)) !== false) { yield $row; }
    } finally { fclose($h); }
}
foreach (readRows('patients.csv') as $row) { /* one row in memory at a time */ }

Generators are PHP's equivalent of a lazy Java Stream/Iterator: ideal for large files or DB cursors. yield from delegates to another generator.

Magic Methods and Superglobals

MethodCalled when
__construct / __destructObject created / destroyed
__get, __set, __isset, __unsetReading/writing an inaccessible or missing property
__call, __callStaticCalling a missing method (used by ORMs, proxies)
__invokeObject used as a function: $obj()
__toStringObject used as a string (implements Stringable)
__cloneAfter clone (shallow copy) — deep-copy nested objects here
__serialize / __unserializeCustom serialisation

Superglobals: $_GET, $_POST, $_COOKIE, $_FILES, $_SERVER, $_SESSION, $_ENV, $_REQUEST (GET+POST+COOKIE — avoid, ambiguous). All are untrusted input except $_SESSION. Modern frameworks wrap them in a PSR-7 request object.

include vs require: require stops with a fatal error if the file is missing, include only warns; the _once variants skip files already loaded. With Composer autoloading you rarely need either except for config and templates.

Secure File Uploads and Unsafe Deserialisation

$f = $_FILES['report'] ?? null;
if (!$f || $f['error'] !== UPLOAD_ERR_OK || $f['size'] > 5_000_000) { throw new RuntimeException('Bad upload'); }
$mime = (new finfo(FILEINFO_MIME_TYPE))->file($f['tmp_name']);   // real type, not the client's claim
$allowed = ['application/pdf' => 'pdf', 'image/png' => 'png', 'image/jpeg' => 'jpg'];
if (!isset($allowed[$mime])) { throw new RuntimeException('Type not allowed'); }
$name = bin2hex(random_bytes(16)) . '.' . $allowed[$mime];       // never trust the original name
move_uploaded_file($f['tmp_name'], '/var/app-uploads/' . $name);  // outside the web root

Never call unserialize() on user input: it can instantiate arbitrary classes and trigger magic methods (PHP object injection, leading to remote code execution via "gadget chains"). Use json_decode, or unserialize($data, ['allowed_classes' => false]) if you must.

Interview Questions — PHP 8 & Twig

What does the PHP request lifecycle look like with Nginx and php-fpm?

Nginx serves static files itself and passes .php requests over FastCGI to a php-fpm pool. A free worker loads the script, which OPcache usually already has in compiled form, runs the bootstrap and autoloader, handles the request and returns the response. Then all request memory is freed. That is the shared-nothing model: nothing survives to the next request except what you store in sessions, a cache or the DB. 💡 When the site gets slow, check pm.max_children and the php-fpm slow log before blaming the code.

What does declare(strict_types=1) do?

It turns off scalar type coercion for function calls made from the file that declares it. Passing "5" to an int parameter then throws TypeError instead of silently converting. It must be the first statement in the file and applies per file, not to the whole project. Return types are checked in strict mode too. 💡 Put it in every new file and enforce it with PHP-CS-Fixer or PHPStan.

Difference between == and ===?

== compares after type juggling. === also requires the same type. PHP 8 made string-to-number comparison saner (0 == "a" is now false), but "1" == "01" and null == false are still true. Use ===, and pass true to in_array()/array_search() for strict checks.

How are PHP arrays different from Java collections?

A PHP array is one ordered hash map that works as a list, map, stack or queue. Keys are int or string, and insertion order is kept. Arrays are passed by value with copy-on-write, so a function that changes an array changes a copy unless the parameter is declared by reference &$arr. Java has separate List/Map/Set types passed by reference. For a typed, mutable collection in PHP you would use a small class or ArrayObject/SPL structures.

Interface vs abstract class vs trait?

An interface is a pure contract, and a class can implement many. An abstract class shares state and partial implementation and allows single inheritance only. A trait is reusable code copied into classes with use. It can hold properties and methods but is not a type, so you cannot type-hint a trait. Typical design: type-hint against interfaces, put shared base behavior in an abstract class, and use traits for small cross-cutting helpers such as timestamps or logging.

What is the difference between self::, static:: and parent::?

self:: resolves to the class where the code is written. static:: uses late static binding and resolves to the class that was actually called, which is what makes return new static() factories work in subclasses. parent:: calls the parent class's implementation, for example parent::__construct().

Explain PSR-4 autoloading and Composer.

Composer reads composer.json, resolves dependency versions, writes composer.lock and generates vendor/autoload.php. With PSR-4, a namespace prefix maps to a folder ("App\\": "src/"), so App\Billing\Invoice loads src/Billing/Invoice.php the first time it is used. That removes manual require calls. 💡 In CI and Docker builds run composer install --no-dev --optimize-autoloader against the committed lock file.

Which PHP 8 features do you use most?

Constructor property promotion and readonly for small immutable DTOs. Enums instead of string constants. match instead of switch, because it compares strictly, returns a value and has no fall-through. The nullsafe operator ?-> for optional relations. Named arguments for functions with many optional parameters. Union types, and attributes for routing or validation metadata.

$label = match (true) {
    $bmi < 18.5 => 'Underweight',
    $bmi < 25   => 'Normal',
    default     => 'Overweight',
};
What are property hooks and asymmetric visibility in PHP 8.4?

Property hooks let a property declare its own get and/or set logic, so you can validate or normalize on write, or compute a virtual property, without writing getter and setter methods. Asymmetric visibility sets read and write scope separately, e.g. public private(set) string $id is publicly readable but only writable inside the class. Together they replace a lot of getter/setter boilerplate, similar to what Kotlin or C# properties give you on the JVM/.NET side.

readonly property vs readonly class vs constant?

A readonly property (8.1) can be set once, from inside the class scope (usually in the constructor). After that, any write throws Error. A readonly class (8.2) makes every declared property readonly and forbids dynamic properties. A class const is a compile-time value shared by all instances, and since 8.3 it can be typed. Note that readonly is shallow: an object stored in a readonly property can still change internally.

Exception vs Error in PHP?

Both implement Throwable. Exception is for recoverable application failures that your code throws and catches. Error comes from the engine: TypeError, ValueError, calling an undefined method, and so on. catch (Exception $e) does not catch an Error, so a top-level handler should catch Throwable. PHP has no checked exceptions; document thrown types with @throws.

How do you prevent SQL injection in PHP?

Use prepared statements with bound parameters (PDO or mysqli) and never build SQL by concatenating user input. Set PDO::ATTR_EMULATE_PREPARES => false so the server does real prepares, and ERRMODE_EXCEPTION. Identifiers (sort column, table) cannot be bound, so whitelist them. 💡 In OpenEMR the equivalent is sqlQuery()/sqlStatement() with ? placeholders and a bind array.

$stmt = $pdo->prepare('SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ?');
$stmt->execute([$email]);
How do you prevent XSS and CSRF?

XSS: escape output for its context. That means HTML body, HTML attribute, JavaScript and URL each need their own escaping. Use htmlspecialchars(..., ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8') or a template engine with autoescape such as Twig, avoid |raw, and add a CSP header. CSRF: give each session a random token, embed it in forms and AJAX headers, and verify it with hash_equals() on every state-changing request. SameSite cookies add a second layer of protection.

How should passwords be stored?

Store them with password_hash($password, PASSWORD_DEFAULT) and check them with password_verify(). This gives a salted, slow hash (bcrypt by default, Argon2id available) with the algorithm and cost stored inside the hash string. Call password_needs_rehash() at login to upgrade old hashes. Never use md5/sha1, never write your own salting scheme, and never log passwords.

How do sessions work and how do you secure them?

session_start() reads or creates a session ID that travels in a cookie, and the data stays on the server in $_SESSION. To secure them, set cookie flags (Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite), enable session.use_strict_mode, call session_regenerate_id(true) on login and privilege change, add idle and absolute timeouts, and fully destroy the session on logout. When running several containers, use a shared session store such as Redis or the DB.

Explain Twig template inheritance and autoescaping.

A base layout defines {% block %} placeholders. A child uses {% extends 'base.html.twig' %}, overrides only the blocks it needs and can call {{ parent() }} to keep the original content. {% include %} and {% embed %} reuse partials, and macros act like template functions. Autoescape is on by default with the HTML strategy, so every {{ }} output is escaped. You can switch strategy per value (|e('js'), |e('url')) or skip escaping with |raw for trusted content only.

How is PHP different from Java for building web apps?

PHP rebuilds the app on every request and scales by adding processes. Java keeps a long-running JVM where singletons, caches and connection pools live in memory. PHP's types are optional and checked at runtime, while Java's are static and checked at compile time. The concepts map closely: Composer↔Maven, Symfony/Laravel↔Spring, PHPUnit↔JUnit, Doctrine↔Hibernate, Twig↔Thymeleaf. 💡 Mention that static analysis (PHPStan/Psalm at a high level) gives PHP code much of the safety you get from the Java compiler.

isset vs empty vs is_null vs ??

isset($x) is true if the variable exists and is not null; it doesn't warn on undefined variables or array keys. empty($x) is true for missing or "falsy" values: null, false, 0, "0", "", [] — so "0" being empty is a classic bug. is_null($x) is true only for null and warns if undefined. $a ?? 'default' uses the default when the left side is unset or null, and ??= assigns only if null.

Closure vs arrow function in PHP?

A closure (function () use ($x) { … }) must list captured variables explicitly with use, by value or by reference (use (&$x)), and can have multiple statements. An arrow function (fn($p) => $p * $rate, PHP 7.4+) captures the outer scope automatically by value and is a single expression — similar to a Java lambda. Since 8.1 the first-class callable syntax strlen(...) creates a closure from any function or method.

What are generators and when would you use them?

A function containing yield returns a Generator that produces values lazily as you iterate. Memory stays constant, so it's ideal for reading big CSVs, paging through DB results or streaming exports. Generators can also receive values (send()), return a final value (getReturn()) and delegate with yield from. They're single-pass, like a Java Iterator.

Are PHP objects and arrays passed by value or by reference?

Arrays are passed by value but with copy-on-write: no copy happens until the function modifies it. Objects are passed as handles (like Java references), so a function can change the object's state but reassigning the parameter doesn't affect the caller. Use &$param for real references — sparingly, and beware the classic bug of a foreach ($arr as &$v) reference left alive after the loop (call unset($v)).

How do you handle file uploads securely?

Check $_FILES[...]['error'] and size, detect the real MIME type with finfo (not the client-supplied type or extension), allow-list types, generate a random file name, and store it outside the web root (or in object storage) with move_uploaded_file. Serve files through a controller that checks authorisation, with Content-Disposition and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff. Also set upload_max_filesize/post_max_size, and scan for malware if users share files.

Why is unserialize() on user input dangerous?

unserialize can create objects of any loaded class and then calls magic methods like __wakeup, __destruct or __toString on them. An attacker can chain existing classes ("gadget chains") to delete files or execute code — PHP object injection, the same class of bug as Java deserialisation vulnerabilities. Use JSON for data exchange, or pass ['allowed_classes' => false], and sign any serialized data you must store client-side.

What does __invoke do and where is it useful?

__invoke lets an object be called like a function ($handler($request)) and makes it a valid callable. It is common for single-action controllers, middleware and command handlers, where the class holds injected dependencies and the call does the work. It's similar to implementing a Java functional interface such as Function.

How do you work with UTF-8 strings correctly in PHP?

Core string functions (strlen, substr, strtoupper) work on bytes, so they break on multibyte characters such as Tamil, Hindi or emoji. Use the mbstring functions (mb_strlen, mb_substr, mb_strtoupper), set the DB connection charset to utf8mb4 (PDO DSN charset=utf8mb4), and send Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8. htmlspecialchars defaults to UTF-8 in PHP 8.

How do you unit test PHP code?

With PHPUnit (or Pest on top of it): test classes extend TestCase, use assertions such as assertSame, data providers for parameterised cases, and test doubles via createMock() (Mockery is an alternative). Write code with constructor injection so dependencies can be replaced, use an in-memory or containerised database for repository tests, and run PHPStan/Psalm static analysis in CI alongside the tests. Xdebug or PCOV provides code coverage.

How do you add a custom filter or function to Twig?

Create an extension class extending AbstractExtension and return TwigFilter/TwigFunction objects from getFilters()/getFunctions(), then register it with the environment ($twig->addExtension(...); Symfony auto-registers it). Output from a filter is auto-escaped unless you declare is_safe => ['html'], which you should only do if the filter itself escapes its input.

class AppExtension extends AbstractExtension {
  public function getFilters(): array {
    return [new TwigFilter('mask_phone', fn(string $p) => str_repeat('*', max(0, strlen($p) - 4)) . substr($p, -4))];
  }
}
// {{ patient.phone|mask_phone }}

OpenEMR, FHIR & Healthcare IT EHR / EMR

OpenEMR is a widely used open-source EHR written in PHP on MySQL/MariaDB. In healthcare IT interviews you will be asked how to customize it safely, how to exchange data with HL7 v2 and FHIR R4, and how to protect patient data under HIPAA.

GET /apis/default/fhir/Observation?patient=123&category=vital-signs&_count=50
Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOi...
Accept: application/fhir+json

{
  "resourceType": "Bundle",
  "type": "searchset",
  "total": 1,
  "entry": [{
    "fullUrl": "https://emr.example.org/apis/default/fhir/Observation/9f1c...",
    "resource": {
      "resourceType": "Observation",
      "id": "9f1c...",
      "status": "final",
      "category": [{ "coding": [{ "system": "http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/observation-category",
                                  "code": "vital-signs" }] }],
      "code": { "coding": [{ "system": "http://loinc.org", "code": "8867-4", "display": "Heart rate" }] },
      "subject": { "reference": "Patient/123" },
      "effectiveDateTime": "2026-03-14T10:30:00Z",
      "valueQuantity": { "value": 72, "unit": "beats/min", "system": "http://unitsofmeasure.org", "code": "/min" }
    }
  }]
}

EHR vs EMR & Clinical Terminology

An EMR (Electronic Medical Record) is the digital chart of one practice or organization. An EHR (Electronic Health Record) holds the same kind of data but is built to be shared across providers and organizations through referrals, labs, HIEs and patient access. People often use the two terms interchangeably, but interviewers like to hear that EHR stresses interoperability.

  • SOAP note: Subjective (what the patient reports: chief complaint, HPI), Objective (vitals, exam, labs), Assessment (diagnoses or differential), Plan (orders, meds, follow-up).
  • Encounter: one visit or interaction. Notes, vitals, diagnoses and billing codes hang off it.
  • CC / HPI / ROS / PMH: chief complaint, history of present illness, review of systems, past medical history.
  • Patient lists: problem list, medication list, allergy list, immunizations. Medication reconciliation compares the lists at each transition of care.
  • Codes: ICD-10-CM (diagnoses), CPT/HCPCS (procedures, billing), SNOMED CT (clinical terms), LOINC (lab and vitals observations), RxNorm (drugs), CVX (vaccines).
  • Revenue cycle: eligibility check (X12 270/271) → charges / superbill → claim (X12 837) → remittance (835/ERA) → patient statements.
  • MRN (medical record number), CCD/C-CDA (clinical summary documents), e-prescribing (NCPDP SCRIPT; EPCS for controlled substances).

OpenEMR Overview

OpenEMR is a free, open-source (GPL) EHR and practice-management system that has been ONC-certified. It is written in PHP, uses MySQL/MariaDB, and is commonly deployed with Apache or in the official Docker images. Main features:

  • Patient demographics, encounters, clinical forms (SOAP, vitals, custom LBF "layout-based forms"), problem/med/allergy lists, clinical decision rules.
  • Scheduling (calendar, appointment categories, recalls), billing (fee sheet, X12 claims, ERA posting), e-prescribing through integrations, lab orders and results.
  • Patient portal for appointments, messages, documents and online forms.
  • REST APIs: a "standard" API and a FHIR R4 API, secured with OAuth2 / SMART on FHIR.
  • Multi-language support (xl() translations), access control (ACL / GACL), and audit logging.

The codebase has both older procedural pages (interface/, library/) and modern namespaced code under src/ (PSR-4 namespace OpenEMR\) with services, Symfony components and Twig templates.

Customizing OpenEMR Safely

The golden rule is to avoid editing core files. Every core change becomes a merge conflict at the next upgrade and can break certified behavior. Prefer extension points, in this order:

  • Configuration first: globals settings, layout-based forms, lists, ACL roles, the menu editor, and the document and template managers.
  • Custom modules (interface/modules/custom_modules/), installed and enabled through the Module Manager. A module's bootstrap file subscribes to OpenEMR's Symfony EventDispatcher events to add menu items, inject UI, react to patient or appointment changes, or register API routes, without touching core.
  • Own namespace and tables: put your classes in your module's namespace and your schema changes in your own tables with install/upgrade SQL scripts. Do not alter core tables when you can avoid it.
  • Reuse core helpers: sqlQuery()/sqlStatement() with bind arrays, escaping helpers (text(), attr(), js_escape(), xlt() for translated text), CsrfUtils for CSRF tokens, and AclMain::aclCheckCore() for permissions.
  • When a core change really is needed, keep it small, document it, and ideally send it upstream as a pull request so you stop carrying a patch.
  • Keep customizations in their own repo or folder, and test upgrades on a copy of production data before rollout.
<?php
// custom module bootstrap (simplified sketch)
use OpenEMR\Menu\MenuEvent;
use Symfony\Component\EventDispatcher\EventDispatcherInterface;

/** @var EventDispatcherInterface $eventDispatcher */
$eventDispatcher->addListener(MenuEvent::MENU_UPDATE, function (MenuEvent $event) {
    $menu = $event->getMenu();
    $item = new stdClass();
    $item->label        = xl('Tenant Reports');
    $item->url          = '/interface/modules/custom_modules/oe-tenant-reports/public/index.php';
    $item->requirement  = 0;
    $item->target       = 'rep';
    $item->menu_id      = 'tenantrep';
    $item->children     = [];
    $item->acl_req      = ['patients', 'demo'];
    // append to the Reports menu, then:
    $event->setMenu($menu);
    return $event;
});

Multi-Tenancy & OpenEMR Sites

OpenEMR supports multisite out of the box. Each tenant is a folder under sites/ (for example sites/default, sites/clinic_a) with its own sqlconf.php (database credentials), configuration and documents directory, and normally its own database. The site ID is chosen at login or from the URL. The APIs include it in the path: /apis/{site}/fhir/..., /oauth2/{site}/token.

The usual SaaS multi-tenancy models are:

  • Database per tenant: strongest isolation and easy per-tenant backup and restore. The cost is more migrations and connections to run. This is what OpenEMR sites use.
  • Schema per tenant: a middle ground.
  • Shared tables with a tenant_id column: cheapest, but every query must be filtered, which is easy to get wrong with PHI.

Operational concerns: running schema upgrades across all tenants, onboarding automation, routing each tenant to the right site, separate encryption keys and document storage per site, per-tenant monitoring, and making sure logs, caches and background jobs never mix tenant data.

HL7 v2 vs FHIR

  • HL7 v2 (since the late 1980s) is pipe-delimited text messages made of segments (MSH header, PID patient, PV1 visit, ORC/OBR order, OBX result). It is event-driven, with message types like ADT^A01 (admit), ADT^A08 (update), ORM^O01/OML (orders) and ORU^R01 (results). It usually travels over MLLP on TCP, and the receiver replies with an ACK. It is still everywhere inside hospitals, but every interface tends to need its own mapping.
  • FHIR (Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources) is a modern HL7 standard: modular resources in JSON/XML over RESTful HTTP, with OAuth2 security, extensions and profiles. It is the basis of US regulatory APIs (ONC Cures Act, CMS interoperability rules).
  • HL7 v3 / CDA: XML clinical documents. C-CDA (CCD, discharge summary, referral note) is still used for document exchange.
MSH|^~\&|LAB|ACME|EMR|CLINIC|20260314103000||ORU^R01|MSG0001|P|2.5.1
PID|1||123^^^CLINIC^MR||DOE^JANE||19800101|F
OBR|1|ORD1001||2345-7^Glucose^LN
OBX|1|NM|2345-7^Glucose^LN||95|mg/dL|70-99|N|||F

FHIR R4 Basics

Everything in FHIR is a resource with a resourceType, an id, meta (versionId, lastUpdated, profile) and typed elements. Resources point to each other with references ("subject": {"reference": "Patient/123"}). Common resources:

  • Patient, Practitioner, PractitionerRole, Organization, Location
  • Encounter (visit), Appointment
  • Condition (problems/diagnoses), AllergyIntolerance, Procedure, Immunization
  • Observation (vitals, labs, social history; coded with LOINC), DiagnosticReport
  • MedicationRequest (prescription/order), MedicationStatement, Medication
  • DocumentReference, Coverage, CarePlan, Provenance

REST interactions: GET [base]/Patient/123 (read), GET [base]/Patient?name=smith (search), POST (create), PUT (update), DELETE, GET [base]/Patient/123/_history. GET [base]/metadata returns the CapabilityStatement (what the server supports). Errors come back as an OperationOutcome. The media type is application/fhir+json.

Search parameters: ?family=doe&birthdate=ge1980-01-01, token search ?identifier=http://hospital/mrn|123, modifiers (:exact, :contains, :missing), and result parameters _count, _sort, _include, _revinclude, _lastUpdated, _elements. Paging uses link[relation=next] URLs.

Bundles group resources. Types: searchset (search results), transaction (all-or-nothing writes), batch (independent writes), collection, document, message, history. Bulk Data ($export) produces NDJSON files for population-level extracts.

SMART on FHIR, OAuth2 Scopes & US Core

SMART on FHIR standardizes how apps launch against and authorize with a FHIR server, using OAuth2 + OpenID Connect. The app reads .well-known/smart-configuration, runs the authorization code flow with PKCE, and receives an access token plus launch context such as the current patient.

  • Launch types: EHR launch (started from inside the EHR with a launch parameter) and standalone launch (launch/patient scope asks the user to pick a patient).
  • Scopes: patient/Observation.read (SMART v1) or patient/Observation.rs (SMART v2, letters from c-r-u-d-s); user/Patient.read; openid fhirUser (identity); offline_access (refresh token).
  • Backend services: system-to-system access with client_credentials and a signed JWT assertion, using system/*.read scopes. Typical for Bulk $export.
  • Apply least privilege: request only the scopes the app needs, keep tokens short-lived, and let the server enforce scopes per resource.

US Core is the set of FHIR R4 profiles (constraints, required "must support" elements, terminology bindings, required search parameters) that US EHRs implement to expose the USCDI data classes for certified API access. A US Core Patient, for example, requires identifier, name and gender, and defines race/ethnicity extensions.

Healthcare Data Security & Compliance

HIPAA (US) protects PHI, meaning health information tied to an identifiable person. Its main parts:

  • Privacy Rule: who may use or disclose PHI, the minimum necessary standard, and patient rights of access.
  • Security Rule: administrative, physical and technical safeguards (access control, audit controls, integrity, authentication, transmission security) for electronic PHI.
  • Breach Notification Rule. HITECH raised the penalties. Vendors handling PHI sign a BAA (Business Associate Agreement), and that includes cloud and AI vendors.

Engineering practices that implement these rules:

  • RBAC with least privilege, unique user IDs, MFA, automatic logoff, and "break-the-glass" emergency access that is logged.
  • Audit logs: who viewed or changed which record, when and from where. Make them append-only and tamper-evident, and review them. OpenEMR has built-in audit logging and an ATNA option.
  • Encryption in transit (TLS 1.2+, HSTS, encrypted DB connections) and at rest (encrypted disks/volumes, encrypted backups, field-level encryption for sensitive data, keys kept in a KMS/vault).
  • No PHI in logs, URLs, error messages, analytics or test fixtures. Use de-identified or synthetic data (e.g. Synthea) outside production.
  • Backups with tested restores, patch management, vulnerability scanning, and a documented incident response plan.

FHIR Data Types, Profiles and Extensions

TypeShapeExample
Codingsystem + code + displayhttp://loinc.org | 2345-7 | Glucose
CodeableConceptOne or more Codings + free textDiagnosis coded in both SNOMED CT and ICD-10
Identifiersystem (namespace URI) + valueMRN, national ID, insurance member number
ReferenceLink to another resource"subject": {"reference": "Patient/123"}
Quantityvalue + unit (UCUM)95 mg/dL
Period, HumanName, Address, ContactPointStructured common dataEncounter start/end, patient name and phone
  • Identifier vs id: id is the server's technical key; identifier is a business ID (MRN). Match and de-duplicate on identifiers, never assume ids are stable across servers.
  • Extensions add data the base spec lacks (e.g. US Core race/ethnicity) via a URL + value; modifierExtension changes meaning and must not be ignored.
  • Profiles (StructureDefinitions, published in Implementation Guides like US Core) constrain resources — required elements, cardinality, value-set bindings. Validate against them with the FHIR validator or HAPI's validation module.

FHIR in Java with HAPI FHIR

HAPI FHIR is the standard Java library: model classes for each FHIR version, JSON/XML parsers, a fluent REST client, validation, and a server framework (plus the ready-made HAPI JPA server).

FhirContext ctx = FhirContext.forR4();     // expensive: create once, reuse (thread-safe)
IGenericClient client = ctx.newRestfulGenericClient("https://fhir.example.com/r4");
client.registerInterceptor(new BearerTokenAuthInterceptor(accessToken));

Bundle bundle = client.search().forResource(Observation.class)
    .where(Observation.SUBJECT.hasId("Patient/123"))
    .and(Observation.CODE.exactly().systemAndCode("http://loinc.org", "2345-7"))
    .sort().descending(Observation.DATE)
    .returnBundle(Bundle.class).execute();

for (Bundle.BundleEntryComponent e : bundle.getEntry()) {
    Observation obs = (Observation) e.getResource();
    System.out.println(obs.getValueQuantity().getValue() + " " + obs.getValueQuantity().getUnit());
}
// follow paging: client.loadPage().next(bundle).execute()

For HL7 v2, the sister library HAPI v2 parses and builds pipe-delimited messages (PipeParser, typed segments like PID, OBX) and supports MLLP. Hospitals often run an interface engine (Mirth Connect / NextGen Connect, Rhapsody) to route, transform and retry messages between systems, including v2 → FHIR mapping.

Patient Matching, De-identification and CDS Hooks

  • Patient matching / MPI: a Master Patient Index links records for the same person across systems using identifiers plus demographics (name, DOB, sex, address, phone), with deterministic rules or probabilistic scoring. Uncertain matches go to a human review queue; duplicates are merged with a link/audit trail, never silently. FHIR offers Patient/$match and Patient.link.
  • De-identification (HIPAA): Safe Harbor removes 18 identifier types (names, most geographic detail, full dates except year, phone, email, MRN, etc.); Expert Determination uses a statistician's assessment of re-identification risk. Pseudonymisation (replacing IDs with tokens) is not full de-identification.
  • CDS Hooks: the EHR calls an external decision-support service at workflow points (patient-view, order-select, order-sign) with FHIR context; the service returns cards (warnings, suggestions, links to SMART apps), such as a drug-interaction alert.

Interview Questions — OpenEMR, FHIR & Healthcare IT

What is the difference between an EMR and an EHR?

An EMR is the digital version of one practice's paper chart, used mostly inside that organization. An EHR covers the same clinical data but is designed to follow the patient across providers through standards-based exchange (FHIR, C-CDA, HIE connections, patient portals). In practice products are called both. 💡 Mention interoperability as the deciding difference.

What is OpenEMR and what is its tech stack?

OpenEMR is an open-source (GPL), ONC-certified EHR and practice-management system. It covers demographics, encounters, clinical forms, scheduling, billing, e-prescribing integrations, lab interfaces and a patient portal. It runs on PHP with MySQL/MariaDB behind Apache, is often deployed with the official Docker images, mixes legacy procedural code with namespaced src/ classes and Twig templates, and offers REST and FHIR R4 APIs secured with OAuth2/SMART.

How do you customize OpenEMR without breaking upgrades?

Configure before you code: globals, layout-based forms, lists, ACLs, menus. For code, build a custom module that hooks into core through Symfony EventDispatcher events and keeps its own namespace, tables and install/upgrade SQL. Reuse core helpers for DB access, escaping, CSRF and ACL checks. Unavoidable core patches should be small, documented and sent upstream where possible. Test every upgrade on a staging copy. 💡 Keeping a list of "core diffs we carry" makes upgrades predictable.

How does OpenEMR support multiple tenants?

Through multisite. Each site lives under sites/<siteid>/ with its own sqlconf.php, configuration and document storage, and usually its own database. The site ID appears in API and OAuth paths (/apis/<site>/fhir). That is database-per-tenant isolation: good for PHI separation and per-tenant restore, with the trade-off that schema upgrades and onboarding have to be automated across all sites.

Compare database-per-tenant with shared-schema tenancy for a healthcare SaaS.

Database per tenant gives strong isolation and simple per-tenant backup and deletion, and it is easier to explain to auditors, but there are more databases to migrate and monitor. Shared schema with tenant_id is cheaper and simpler to run, but a single missing WHERE tenant_id = ? leaks PHI. If you choose it, enforce the filter centrally (repository layer or row-level security) and test for it. For PHI, many teams accept the operational cost of database-per-tenant.

HL7 v2 vs FHIR — when would you use each?

HL7 v2 is pipe-delimited, event-driven messaging (ADT, ORM/OML, ORU) over MLLP. It remains the standard for in-hospital feeds such as lab results and admissions, often routed through an interface engine. FHIR is resource-based REST/JSON with OAuth2, suited to apps, patient access, payer APIs and regulatory requirements. Real systems often use both: v2 feeds come in, are mapped to FHIR resources, and are exposed through a FHIR API.

Name key FHIR resources and what they represent.

Patient (demographics), Practitioner/Organization (providers), Encounter (a visit), Condition (problem/diagnosis), Observation (vitals, labs, smoking status), MedicationRequest (prescription), AllergyIntolerance, Immunization, Procedure, DiagnosticReport, DocumentReference, Appointment. They link by references, e.g. an Observation's subject → Patient and encounter → Encounter.

How does FHIR search work? Give examples.

Search is GET [base]/[Type]?params and returns a searchset Bundle with paging links. Each resource defines its own parameters, and prefixes and modifiers refine them.

GET /Patient?family=doe&birthdate=ge1980-01-01
GET /Observation?patient=123&code=http://loinc.org|8867-4&_sort=-date&_count=10
GET /MedicationRequest?patient=123&status=active&_include=MedicationRequest:medication
GET /Encounter?patient=123&date=ge2026-01-01&_revinclude=Observation:encounter

💡 Check the server's CapabilityStatement (/metadata) to see which search parameters it actually supports.

What is a FHIR Bundle and what types exist?

A Bundle is a container of resource entries. searchset holds search results. transaction is processed atomically, all or nothing, and can use temporary urn:uuid references between new resources. batch runs each entry independently. document starts with a Composition. message starts with a MessageHeader. history lists versions, and collection is a plain grouping.

What is SMART on FHIR and how do scopes work?

SMART on FHIR is a profile of OAuth2/OIDC for healthcare apps. The app discovers endpoints from .well-known/smart-configuration, runs the authorization code flow with PKCE (EHR or standalone launch), and gets a token with launch context such as the patient ID. Scopes have the form context/Resource.permissions: patient/Observation.read in v1, patient/Observation.rs in v2, user/*.read, and system/*.read for backend services. Add openid fhirUser for identity and offline_access for refresh tokens.

What is US Core?

US Core is the HL7 implementation guide of FHIR R4 profiles that defines the minimum US data (aligned with USCDI). It specifies which elements are required or must be supported, which terminology to use (LOINC, SNOMED CT, RxNorm) and which searches servers must support. Certified EHR APIs are tested against it, so a US Core-conformant client can work with many EHRs with little custom mapping.

Which HIPAA safeguards do you implement as a developer?

Technical safeguards: unique logins and RBAC with least privilege, MFA, session timeouts, audit logs of PHI access and changes, integrity controls, and encryption in transit (TLS) and at rest (encrypted disks, DB and backups, keys in a KMS). On top of that: no PHI in logs, URLs or test data, prepared statements and output escaping, dependency patching, and BAAs with any vendor (cloud, email, AI) that touches PHI. 💡 Also mention the "minimum necessary" principle when designing APIs and reports.

What should an audit log in an EHR capture?

Who (user ID and role), what (action: view, create, update, delete, print, export), which record (patient and resource ID), when (UTC timestamp), where (IP, device, client app), and the outcome (success or denied). Include "break-the-glass" overrides. Logs should be append-only, tamper-evident, retained according to policy, searchable for patient-access reports, and they must not contain more PHI than needed.

How do you escape output and protect forms in OpenEMR code?

Use the core helpers: text() for HTML body text, attr() inside attributes, js_escape() for JavaScript values, and xlt()/xla() to translate and escape in one step. In Twig templates autoescape does this for you. Add a CSRF token (CsrfUtils::collectCsrfToken()) to forms and verify it on submit. Check permissions with the ACL API before reading or writing PHI, and use bound parameters in every SQL call.

Explain the SOAP note.

SOAP is the standard structure for documenting an encounter. Subjective: the patient's own account (chief complaint, HPI, symptoms). Objective: measurable findings (vitals, exam, lab results). Assessment: the clinician's diagnosis or differential. Plan: treatment, prescriptions, orders, education, follow-up. In an EMR, the assessment usually maps to ICD-10 codes and the plan to orders and MedicationRequests.

Walk through a typical outpatient clinical workflow in an EMR.

Scheduling, then eligibility check, then check-in (demographics, insurance, consent), then intake (vitals, medication and allergy reconciliation), then the provider encounter (SOAP note, diagnoses, orders, e-prescriptions), then checkout (follow-up appointment, patient summary or portal access), then coding and charge capture, then claim submission and payment posting. Lab results come back, often over HL7 v2, and are filed and reviewed against the encounter.

What is a CodeableConcept, and why can it hold several codings?

A CodeableConcept represents a coded meaning: an array of coding entries (each with system, code, display) plus optional text. Several codings let the same concept be sent in multiple code systems — for example SNOMED CT for clinical use and ICD-10-CM for billing — or a local code with its standard equivalent. Receivers should match on system + code, never on display text.

How do you prevent two users from overwriting each other's update to a FHIR resource?

Use optimistic locking: the server returns the resource's meta.versionId as an ETag (e.g. W/"3"). The client sends If-Match: W/"3" on its PUT; if someone else updated it first, the server responds 412 Precondition Failed and the client re-reads and merges. This is the FHIR equivalent of JPA's @Version. Version history is available via _history.

What are conditional create and conditional update in FHIR?

Conditional create sends If-None-Exist: identifier=http://hospital/mrn|12345 with a POST, so the server creates the resource only if no match exists — this avoids duplicates when a message is retried. Conditional update is PUT Patient?identifier=...: it updates the single match or creates one if none exists, and fails if several match. Both make integrations idempotent, which matters because interfaces retry.

How would you consume or expose FHIR from a Spring Boot application?

Use HAPI FHIR. As a client: create one FhirContext.forR4() bean (it is expensive and thread-safe), build an IGenericClient, add an auth interceptor with a SMART/OAuth2 token, and use the fluent search API, following Bundle paging links. As a server: either implement IResourceProvider classes over your own database with HAPI's RestfulServer servlet, or deploy the HAPI JPA server. Validate incoming resources against the relevant profiles (US Core or your own).

How do you integrate an HL7 v2 lab feed into a Java system?

Messages usually arrive over MLLP (TCP with start/end framing bytes), often via an interface engine such as Mirth Connect. In Java, use HAPI v2 to parse the ORU^R01 message, read PID for the patient and OBR/OBX for orders and results, and return an ACK (AA accept, AE/AR error/reject) so the sender knows whether to retry. Store or map results to FHIR Observation/DiagnosticReport, match the patient by MRN, and keep the raw message for audit and replay. Make processing idempotent on the message control ID (MSH-10).

How do you handle duplicate patient records?

Prevent them first: search before registration on identifiers and demographics (name, DOB, phone), with fuzzy matching on names. Use an MPI or matching service that scores candidates; auto-link only high-confidence matches and send the rest to a review queue. Merging must keep a full audit trail, re-point encounters, orders and results to the surviving record, and be reversible (unmerge), because a wrong merge mixes two people's clinical data — a patient-safety issue.

What is the difference between de-identification and pseudonymisation?

De-identified data (HIPAA Safe Harbor: remove 18 identifier types; or Expert Determination) is no longer PHI and can be used for analytics with fewer restrictions. Pseudonymised data replaces identifiers with tokens but can be re-linked with a key, so it is still regulated (and is still personal data under GDPR). For dev and test environments, prefer synthetic data (for example Synthea) over masked copies of production.

What is Patient/$everything and when would you use it?

GET Patient/123/$everything is a FHIR operation that returns a Bundle with the patient and all related resources the server holds (encounters, conditions, observations, medications…), optionally limited by _since, _type or date range. It is useful for patient record exports or transferring a chart. For whole populations, use Bulk Data $export instead, which produces NDJSON files asynchronously.

What is CDS Hooks?

A standard for plugging clinical decision support into the EHR workflow. At defined hooks such as patient-view or order-sign, the EHR POSTs context (patient, draft orders, prefetched FHIR data) to a CDS service, which returns cards: information, warnings, suggested actions or a link to launch a SMART app. Examples: drug–allergy interaction warnings, overdue screening reminders. Services must respond fast (sub-second) because they sit in the clinician's workflow.

Besides HIPAA, which regulations might a healthcare app need to consider?

In the US, the 21st Century Cures Act requires certified EHRs to offer standard FHIR APIs and prohibits information blocking (unreasonably preventing access to or exchange of health data); ONC certification criteria define the details. In the EU, GDPR treats health data as a special category requiring explicit legal basis, data minimisation and breach notification within 72 hours. In India, the DPDP Act governs personal data and ABDM defines health IDs (ABHA) and FHIR-based exchange. 💡 Mention whichever applies to the market you worked in, and the controls you implemented.

Interview Questions — Commands

git merge vs git rebase — when do you use each?

Merge joins histories with a merge commit and never rewrites anything, so it is safe on shared branches. Rebase replays your commits on top of another branch for a linear history; use it on your own feature branch before opening a PR (git pull --rebase, git rebase -i to squash). 💡 Golden rule: never rebase commits that others have already pulled.

git reset vs git revert?

reset moves the branch pointer back (soft keeps changes staged, mixed keeps them unstaged, hard discards them) and rewrites history — fine locally. revert adds a new commit that undoes an earlier one, so it is the safe way to undo something already pushed to a shared branch.

You committed a password and pushed it. What do you run?

First rotate the secret — assume it is compromised. Then remove it from history with git filter-repo --path secrets.env --invert-paths (or BFG), force-push, and ask everyone to re-clone. Add the file to .gitignore and a pre-commit secret scanner so it cannot happen again.

npm install vs npm ci?

npm install may update package-lock.json within allowed ranges. npm ci deletes node_modules and installs exactly what the lock file says, failing if it is out of sync — reproducible and faster, so it is what CI pipelines (Jenkins) should use.

A Spring Boot service is using 100% CPU in production. Which commands do you run?

top -H -p <pid> to find the hot thread id, convert it to hex (printf '%x' <tid>), then jstack <pid> and search for that nid to see the stack. Take 2–3 thread dumps a few seconds apart; also check GC with jstat -gcutil <pid> 1000 — constant full GCs look like CPU load too.

How do you debug a container that keeps restarting?

docker ps -a for the exit code (137 = killed, often OOM; 1 = app error), docker logs --tail 200 <c> for the stack trace, and docker inspect <c> for env vars, mounts and OOMKilled. In Kubernetes: kubectl describe pod (events) and kubectl logs --previous.

Port 8080 is already in use. How do you find and stop the process?

Linux/macOS: lsof -i :8080 or ss -tulpn | grep 8080, then kill -15 <pid> (and -9 only if it will not stop). Windows: netstat -ano | findstr :8080, then taskkill /PID <pid> /F.

kill -15 vs kill -9?

SIGTERM (15) asks the process to shut down — Spring Boot runs its graceful shutdown, finishes in-flight requests and closes connection pools. SIGKILL (9) cannot be caught; the JVM dies immediately with no cleanup. Always try 15 first; Docker stop sends SIGTERM then SIGKILL after the timeout.

How do you find which dependency pulls in a conflicting library version?

Maven: mvn dependency:tree -Dincludes=group:artifact; Gradle: ./gradlew dependencyInsight --dependency artifact. Then pin the version in dependencyManagement / a platform BOM or add an exclusion.

docker compose down vs docker compose down -v?

Both stop and remove containers and networks; -v also deletes named volumes — i.e. your database data. Use plain down (or restart) unless you deliberately want a clean database.

How do you see the last 100 errors in a log file and count them by type?

grep "ERROR" app.log | tail -n 100 for the latest ones, and grep -o "[A-Za-z.]*Exception" app.log | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr to count exceptions by type. Add -C 5 to grep to see surrounding lines.

How do you upgrade an Angular project to the next major version?

Upgrade one major at a time: ng update @angular/core@18 @angular/cli@18 (then third-party libs like Material), commit, run tests, and repeat. The command runs migration schematics that rewrite code automatically; check the Angular update guide for manual steps.

Thread states (Thread.State)

StateEntered byLeaves by
NEWnew Thread()start()
RUNNABLEstart(); running or ready, includes blocking socket I/OScheduler, lock, wait, end of run()
BLOCKEDWaiting for a synchronized monitorGets the monitor
WAITINGwait(), join(), LockSupport.park()notify(), thread end, unpark()

sleep keeps locks · wait releases the monitor and needs it held · ReentrantLock waiters show as WAITING, not BLOCKED · virtual threads: Java 21.

Garbage collectors

CollectorFlagGoalNote
Serial-XX:+UseSerialGCSmall heap, 1 CPUChosen on small machines and containers
Parallel-XX:+UseParallelGCThroughputStop-the-world, batch jobs

CMS removed in 14 · Young (Eden, S0, S1), Old · Metaspace replaced PermGen in 8 · minor GC vs mixed vs full · -Xms -Xmx -Xss · -Xlog:gc* · jcmd, jstack, jmap, JFR.

Observability and cloud at a glance

QuestionAnswer in one breath
Logs vs metrics vs tracesLogs = what happened (Splunk) · metrics = how much/how fast (Prometheus, Micrometer) · traces = where time went across services (OpenTelemetry, Sentry) · tie them with a trace/correlation ID in MDC
Sentry vs SplunkSentry = grouped exceptions with context and alerts per issue · Splunk = search across all log events
SLI / SLO / error budgetMeasured good ratio / target (99.9%) / allowed failure (≈ 43 min per 30 days at 99.9%)

GCP compute choiceContainer + HTTP + stateless → Cloud Run · full control/VM → Compute Engine · many services, custom networking → GKE · event glue → Cloud Run functions
Secrets anywhereSecret Manager / Vault / Jenkins credentials → injected at runtime · never in Git, images or logs · rotate on leak
